record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Construct the finite-volume correlation functions of four-dimensional Yang-Mills theory in a standard gauge such as Landau gauge, which the paper says likely requires a direct treatment of the Gribov problem.

evidence.quote: Construct the Yang Mills 4 correlation functions in a finite volume and a standard gauge (such as the Landau gauge). This presumably implies a front attack on the Gribov problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a compact, simple, simply connected Lie group (for instance $G=SU(N)$ with $N\ge 2$) with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ equipped with an Ad-invariant inner product. On a finite four-dimensional torus $\Lambda = (\mathbb{R}/L\mathbb{Z})^4$, consider $\mathfrak{g}$-valued connection one-forms $A = \sum_{\mu=1}^{4} A_\mu\, dx^\mu$ with curvature $F_{\mu\nu} = \partial_\mu A_\nu - \partial_\nu A_\mu + [A_\mu, A_\nu]$, and the Yang–Mills action
$$ S_{\mathrm{YM}}(A) = \frac{1}{4g^2}\int_\Lambda \langle F_{\mu\nu}, F^{\mu\nu}\rangle\, d^4x. $$
The action is invariant under gauge transformations $A_\mu \mapsto U^{-1} A_\mu U + U^{-1}\partial_\mu U$ with $U:\Lambda\to G$ smooth. To define a probability measure one must fix a gauge; the Landau gauge imposes $\partial^\mu A_\mu = 0$, but the Gribov phenomenon shows that the Landau gauge slice intersects gauge orbits in more than one point, so a global gauge-fixing on $\Lambda$ is obstructed.

Problem. Construct, in a mathematically rigorous sense (e.g. as a Borel probability measure on a suitable space of distributional connections modulo gauge, or equivalently as a family of gauge-fixed correlation functions satisfying appropriate Osterwalder–Schrader-type properties at finite volume), the finite-volume Euclidean correlation functions of four-dimensional Yang–Mills theory on $\Lambda$ in a standard covariant gauge such as the Landau gauge. In particular, give a non-perturbative definition of the gauge-fixed expectations
$$ \langle A_{\mu_1}(x_1)\cdots A_{\mu_n}(x_n)\rangle_{\Lambda, \text{Landau}} $$
that properly accounts for the Gribov ambiguity (e.g. by restriction to a fundamental modular domain or by an alternative resolution), and prove the existence of these correlation functions for all $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The rigorous construction of four-dimensional Yang–Mills correlation functions, even at finite volume in a fixed covariant gauge, remains an open problem in constructive quantum field theory; it is closely tied to the Clay Millennium Yang–Mills mass-gap problem and to the unresolved Gribov ambiguity. No accepted construction in the Landau gauge at finite volume has appeared in the literature as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Yang–Mills existence and mass gap
status_evidence.snippet: Prove that for any compact simple gauge group G, a non-trivial quantum Yang–Mills theory exists on R^4 and has a mass gap.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of 4D Yang–Mills correlation functions is an open Millennium Problem.

status_evidence.title: Gribov problem (review)
status_evidence.snippet: The Gribov ambiguity obstructs a global covariant gauge fixing in non-abelian gauge theories and remains an active topic of investigation.
status_evidence.claim: The Gribov problem in Landau gauge is unresolved at a rigorous level.
